title: Poor Feeding

rationale.ELIMINATE galactose: soy formula: Lifelong. No breast milk or cow's milk.

hpi: {{patient_name}} is a neonate presenting with poor feeding, vomiting, jaundice, lethargy, and failure to thrive after initiating breast milk or cow's milk formula feeds. Galactosemia is an autosomal recessive deficiency of galactose-1-phosphate uridylyltransferase (GALT) → inability to metabolize galactose → accumulation of galactose-1-phosphate (toxic to liver, brain, kidneys, lens). Classic findings: jaundice (unconjugated progressing to conjugated), hepatomegaly, cataracts (galactitol accumulation in lens), E. coli sepsis (increased risk), renal tubular dysfunction. Newborn screening detects elevated galactose. Confirm: GALT enzyme activity in RBCs. Treatment: ELIMINATE galactose from diet — soy formula instead of milk. Lifelong. Even with treatment, some may have long-term complications (cognitive, ovarian failure).
